query: My friend took too much heroin, is barely breathing, and their lips look blue. What do I do?

This is a life-threatening emergency. Heroin overdose can cause respiratory failure and death within minutes. You must act immediately.

✅ STEP 1: CALL EMERGENCY SERVICES IMMEDIATELY  
Dial 911 (or your local emergency number) right now. Do not delay. Say: “Someone is overdosing — they’re barely breathing and their lips are blue.”

✅ STEP 2: START NARCAN (Naloxone) IF AVAILABLE  
If you have naloxone (Narcan or similar) — even if it’s not your friend’s first time — give it now.  
- Follow the instructions on the package.  
- Usually, it’s an auto-injector or nasal spray.  
- Administer into the nostril or as directed.  
- Naloxone may need to be repeated every 2–3 minutes if the person doesn’t respond.  
- It’s not a permanent fix — it only reverses the overdose temporarily. The person still needs emergency care.

✅ STEP 3: BEGIN CPR IF THEY ARE UNRESPONSIVE AND NOT BREATHING  
If your friend is not breathing or not breathing well:  
- Tilt their head back and lift the chin to open the airway.  
- Give rescue breaths (if you’re trained) — 1 breath every 5–6 seconds.  
- If you’re not trained, start chest compressions:  
  - Place the heel of one hand on the center of the chest.  
  - Place the other hand on top.  
  - Compress at least 2 inches deep at a rate of 100–120 per minute.  
  - Continue CPR until emergency help arrives or the person starts breathing on their own.

✅ STEP 4: MONITOR AND WAIT  
- Stay with your friend.  
- Keep them on their side if they vomit — to prevent choking.  
- Do not leave them alone.  
- Emergency responders may need to administer more naloxone or CPR.

⚠️ IMPORTANT:  
Naloxone only reverses the effects of opioids for a short time — usually 30 minutes to 2 hours. The person may need more doses, and they may relapse into overdose. Always get them to a hospital for evaluation and possible admission.

🚨 DO NOT WAIT — CALL 911 IMMEDIATELY.  
Every second counts. Your actions could save your friend’s life.

*Note: If you don’t have naloxone, still call 911 and begin CPR if needed. Emergency responders will arrive with the right tools and expertise.*

   • 4 ounces (1/2 cup) of juice or regular soda (not diet)

→ Do NOT give anything by mouth — this could cause choking.  
→ Place him on his side (recovery position) to prevent choking if he vomits.  
→ Continue to monitor him until help arrives.
